note: Shared expected values for focusSlices() / focus_slices() / __capRsvp.focusSlices — the
FOURTH RSVP fixture, read by backend/tests/test_rsvp_core.py,
src/renderer/src/lib/rsvp.test.ts and src/renderer/src/lib/rsvp.embedded.test.ts. Never
hand-write an expected slice in a suite; add a case here so all three languages are pinned
by the same strings.
focusSlices splits the ACTIVE word into the three pieces every renderer draws separately:
everything before the focus glyph, the focus glyph, everything after. Pillow draws three
Pillow pieces, the Canvas preview draws three fillText calls and the HTML layer emits three
<span>s, so the split has to live in one place per language or the rule gets hand-rolled a
fourth time and drifts.
The contract under test is that the split is in Unicode CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 code units
(backend/exporters/rsvp.py is the reference; both JS copies normalize with Array.from). A
code-unit implementation cuts an astral glyph in half: 'a\ud83c\udfacb' sliced at unit 1
yields focus = the lone HIGH surrogate and suffix = the LOW surrogate + 'b' — two tofu
glyphs on screen and a wrong pivot. 7 of the 14 cases below fail such an implementation
(8 when its orpIndex counts code units too).
prefix + focus + suffix must always rebuild the token; each suite asserts that separately,
derived rather than restated, so it also covers the cases listed here.
f: null means 'derive it with orpIndex(token)', which covers the composition of the two
functions end to end. A number is passed through verbatim (clamping included).
Fixture keys are deliberately camelCase in EVERY rsvp_*.json file — one shape read by both
a Python suite and two TS suites, so the Python side reads case["wordX"] rather than each
language getting its own casing. Do NOT 'fix' these to snake_case: it breaks two suites.

cases.name: ASCII control
cases.why: 'the' with f 1 splits into 't' / 'h' / 'e' — the same arithmetic the astral cases use

cases.name: f = 0 leaves an empty prefix
cases.why: the first glyph is the focus, so there is nothing before it — no undefined, no off-by-one

cases.name: f at the last character leaves an empty suffix
cases.why: the mirror of the f = 0 case; the suffix slice must not wrap around

cases.name: empty token yields three empty strings
cases.why: nothing to split; must not return undefined for the focus (which would draw 'undefined')

cases.name: astral focus char, ASCII on both sides
cases.why: 'a🎬b' -> f 1 is the EMOJI, whole. A code-unit impl yields focus = the lone HIGH surrogate and suffix = the LOW surrogate + 'b'

cases.name: astral in the PREFIX, ASCII focus and suffix
cases.why: 'ab🎬cd' with f 3 puts the whole emoji in the prefix. A code-unit impl cuts it: prefix 'ab' + HIGH surrogate, focus = the LOW one

cases.name: astral in the SUFFIX only
cases.why: 'ab🎬cd' -> f 1, so the emoji sits untouched in the suffix. Both indexings slice the same HERE — the case exists so a suffix pair is pinned as whole; it fails an impl whose orpIndex also counts code units (f 2)

cases.name: all-astral token, derived f
cases.why: '𝔘𝔫𝔦' is 3 code points -> f 1. A code-unit impl splits '𝔘' itself in half and puts '𝔫𝔦' in the suffix

cases.name: all-astral token, explicit last index
cases.why: f 2 of 3 code points: prefix is two whole glyphs and the suffix is empty. A code-unit impl reads unit 2 = the HIGH surrogate of '𝔫'

cases.name: astral across a breakpoint, derived f
cases.why: '🚀…abcdef' is 13 code points -> f 3, the fourth rocket. A code-unit impl lands inside the second rocket

cases.name: out-of-range f clamps in code points
cases.why: '🎬' is ONE unit, so f 5 clamps to 0 and the whole emoji is the focus. A code-unit impl clamps to 1 and focuses the LOW surrogate

cases.name: negative f clamps to 0
cases.why: the low end of the same clamp; must not slice from the end of the token

cases.name: unpaired surrogate is one whole unit
cases.why: MALFORMED but documented: 'a\ud83cb' -> f 1 is the lone surrogate itself. Both indexings agree here — the point is that it can never be split, dropped or merged with a neighbour

cases.name: unpaired surrogate beside a real pair
cases.why: MALFORMED: '\ud83c' + '🎬' is 2 code points, so f 1 is the whole emoji. A code-unit impl focuses the emoji's HIGH surrogate and leaves the LOW one as the suffix
